source_name: Statistično poročilo o oddanih javnih naročilih (MJU annual procurement statistics)
why_relevant: Annual official statistical report on awarded public contracts — gives market sizing, share by procedure type and category, useful for framing how large the addressable Slovenian public-sector spend is in IT/financial services.

source_name: Državni svet / Državni zbor RS – opinions on DKOM and KPK annual reports
why_relevant: Parliamentary/second-chamber opinions on the review body's annual report add critical commentary and sometimes name systemic problem areas (sectors with recurring disputes, capacity constraints) that the body itself understates.

source_name: KPK – Analiza korupcijskih tveganj v postopkih javnega naročanja
why_relevant: Systemic KPK analysis of corruption risks in procurement procedures – gives the typology of manipulations (spec-tailoring, split contracts, single-bid awards) that an analyst should look for when reading award notices for bank/payment contracts, and often cites concrete case material.

source_name: ZJN-3 — Zakon o javnem naročanju (consolidated text, PISRS)
why_relevant: Defines what must be published, by whom, in what form and within what deadlines (e.g. award notice within 30 days of contract conclusion), and how banking/financial service contract values are estimated (on the basis of fees/commissions). This is the ground truth for interpreting completeness and for detecting when a notice is missing.

source_name: Bankart – Letno poročilo (annual reports, incl. English editions)
why_relevant: Bankart annual reports enumerate the ATM fleet composition by manufacturer (NCR, Wincor Nixdorf, Diebold, Diebold Nixdorf) and describe major platform projects — an indirect but datable record of which hardware/software vendors hold the Slovenian processing estate.

source_name: IPRS – Vodnik po praksi ZDIJZ (15 let ZDIJZ guide, PDF)
why_relevant: Case-law digest of 15 years of FOI practice; the fastest way to learn which contract categories (including with commercial banks and payment providers) have been ruled disclosable, and on what reasoning.

source_name: OTP banka Slovenija – Politika skladnosti poslovanja Skupine OTP Slovenija (supplier due-diligence provisions)
why_relevant: Published OTP Slovenia compliance policy stating that compliance performs due-diligence reviews of suppliers to mitigate corruption risk in supplier relationships — the only concrete published OTP SI procurement-governance text located. OTP SI now absorbs the former NKBM and SKB books, so it governs the second-largest bank's vendor onboarding.

source_name: Delavska hranilnica – javne objave / javna povabila (document directory)
why_relevant: Evidence that DH publishes 'javno povabilo za zbiranje zavezujočih ponudb' documents under a dedicated /doc/obvestila-javne-objave/ path (observed instance: purchase of business premises in Izola). This directory is where any DH open market call — including procurement-type invitations — would land, even though the visible Obvestila page carries only customer notices.

source_name: Bank general terms & conditions PDFs (splošni pogoji) – card and payment services
why_relevant: Issuer T&Cs name the schemes, processors and card products in force at each bank and are re-issued when a processing or scheme arrangement changes — a dated, verifiable indirect signal of vendor/scheme switches that are never announced.

source_name: NLB – Politika trajnostnega razvoja (sustainability policy PDF, supplier selection & evaluation framework)
why_relevant: States NLB Group's framework for selecting and regularly evaluating suppliers and supply-chain human-rights expectations — the closest published statement of NLB's procurement rules, useful to infer qualification criteria a vendor must satisfy.

source_name: Printec – NLB case study gated download
why_relevant: Full PDF case study of the NLB contactless-ATM programme; the richest single supplier-side artefact found for Slovenia. Gated behind a lead-capture form.

entity_name: Bank-published counterparty documents naming the vendor
source_name: Bank-published counterparty documents naming the vendor (e.g. BKS Bank BizzNet terms, UniCredit Hal E-Bank manuals)
why_relevant: Slovenian banks' general terms (splošni pogoji) and user manuals for e-banking name the supplying vendor and product explicitly (Halcom Hal E-Bank / Web E-Bank / MultiPay at BKS Bank and UniCredit). This is the most reliable public proof of an installed vendor at a private bank where no tender exists.

source_name: European Payments Council – Slovenia instant-payment environment insight
why_relevant: Documents that in 2018 all Slovenian PSPs agreed to establish Flik as the domestic instant-payment scheme and tracks SCT Inst adherence — the scheme-governance timeline that dates each national implementation programme and its vendor demand.

source_name: Global Public Procurement Database (GPPD) — Slovenia country profile
why_relevant: World Bank-backed comparative profile of Slovenia's procurement system and data availability. Good for framing legal/institutional context and for validating what data is officially supposed to be published.

source_name: Odvetnik Marovt — procurement law firm blog ('Kaj je v ponudbi javno?')
why_relevant: Specialist procurement lawyer explains exactly which bid data (unit prices, total contract value) are public after award — directly governs what a collector can lawfully expect to obtain from Slovene tender files.

source_name: Slovenian government contract-partner disclosure lists (vladna gradiva PDF)
why_relevant: Government contract-partner schedules enumerate Slovenian IT suppliers (RRC, MAOP, SRC, Unistar LC, S&T Slovenija, NIL, Smartis) with contract references. These are public-sector contracts, but they build the supplier actor map and confirm which integrators are capable of banking-scale core/system work.

source_name: TED Developer Docs (docs.ted.europa.eu) — API and Open Data Service guides
why_relevant: Authoritative documentation for query syntax, field names, eForms field IDs, pagination and versioning. Required to write correct CPV/country expert queries and to keep the collector working across TED API versions.

Named vendor success story documenting NLB's core-banking platform and the 2023 migration of N Banka (ex-Sberbank Slovenia) onto it — an award/scope record for the largest core-banking footprint in Slovenia.

source_name: ZBS YouTube channel – Bančna konferenca session recordings
why_relevant: Full recordings of the Slovenian Banking Conference are published publicly. Spoken remarks in panels are markedly less filtered than written materials and often name in-flight platform projects that appear in no agenda text.
